description: Install PAN for OpenCode locally and confirm OpenCode 2 (the `opencode2` binary from npm @opencode/cli) loads PAN's MCP server, agents and plugin.
why: Reality check RC3 (2026-10-19): the 3.35.0 changelog said OpenCode 2 loads PAN's plugin on the strength of a simulated loader, while Homebrew Core has installed OpenCode 2 since 2026-09-28. live-gate-opencode is shaped for 1.x: OpenCode 2 has no `agent list` (it is `debug agents`), and its `debug config` lists config sources, not plugin paths. Measured on 2.0.32 (2026-10-19, R51): v2 normalised PAN's v1 config in memory, `mcp list` showed `pan connected` once the background service was up (the first call raced its start and reported no servers), `debug agents` listed every pan-* agent with the legacy permission keys translated (bash to shell, write to edit, task to subagent), and `plugin list --builtin` listed `pan-wizard` as a local plugin. The @opencode/cli package installs `opencode2` beside `opencode`, so this gate needs no PATH trick; SKIPPED with reason when it is absent.

steps.why: PAN writes the v1 shape on purpose (the published schema is still v1; MI-038); OpenCode 2 must translate it.
Pins the OpenCode 2 build the measurement was taken on.
These subcommands go through OpenCode 2's background service and refuse --standalone.

Right after the service starts it answers before it has loaded the project (on 2.0.32 the first two debug agents calls listed only built-ins); this step waits until PAN's agents are visible so the checks below measure PAN, not the race.
OpenCode 2 lists the servers it loaded for this workspace from PAN's v1 `mcp` block (normalised to `mcp.servers`).
OpenCode 2 loads PAN's agents from .opencode/agents/ and translates their legacy `permission:` frontmatter; `agent list` no longer exists.
The v2 loader registers PAN's plugin under the `id` it exports (R45); plain `plugin list` shows package plugins only.

controls.why: With PAN's MCP server registered under another name, the registration assertion and `opencode2 mcp list` must both fail.
